question.text: Satpura AI-only Fund is a converted Cat II LVF, earlier operating as a regular Cat II AIF with an already-approved 2-year extension. Post-conversion, the Manager proposes a further 5-year extension. How should this be applied?

answer.text: Fresh 5-year extension window over and above the earlier 2 years
No extension permitted post-conversion to AI-only
The 5-year extension shall also INCLUDE any tenure extensions granted prior to conversion — i.e. total post-conversion extension capped at 5 years inclusive
Extension is automatic; no unit-holder consent required

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per the AI-only Fund framework: AI-only Funds may be permitted to extend tenure up to 5 YEARS, subject to 2/3 unit-holder approval. However, for a CONVERTED AI-only Fund/LVF, the 5-year extension shall ALSO INCLUDE any tenure extensions granted prior to conversion. So the cap is inclusive — not additive. This prevents schemes from gaming the conversion to stack 2+5 extensions on top of original tenure. **The Trap:** Option A stacks extensions additively (a common gaming trap). Option B denies extension outright. Option D bypasses the 2/3 consent requirement. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C tests LVF conversion. Extension math is unique to converted funds. Mutual Funds have no analogous conversion-extension rule. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** When advising a converting Cat II AIF, pre-compute the effective remaining extension headroom after accounting for any prior extensions. If you've already used 2 years pre-conversion, only 3 years are available post-conversion under the 5-year inclusive cap. Communicate this upfront to AIs in the consent package.
